findings.title: Fallback locales are only preloaded in controller context, not in background jobs or mailers
findings.body: `ensure_loaded!` is only invoked from `ApplicationController#set_locale` (a before_filter). In contexts outside the request/response cycle—background jobs (Sidekiq), mailers, rake tasks, the Rails console—the fallback locales returned by `FallbackLocaleList#[]` are never loaded via `I18n.ensure_loaded!`. When the i18n Fallbacks module attempts to look up a missing key in a fallback locale, that locale's YAML translations will not have been loaded by the translate_accelerator's lazy-loading mechanism, so the lookup returns nil and the fallback silently fails, producing a missing-translation string instead of the intended fallback value.

findings.title: FallbackLocaleList#[] allocates a new array on every translation lookup
findings.body: The `[]` method builds a fresh array (`[locale, SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym, :en].uniq.compact`) on every invocation. The i18n Fallbacks module calls `I18n.fallbacks[locale]` on every single translation lookup. In a high-traffic Discourse instance this creates significant GC pressure. The result should be memoized (e.g., store in the underlying Hash via `super` or a local cache) and invalidated only when `SiteSetting.default_locale` changes.

findings.title: Non-atomic initialization of @loaded_locales in ensure_loaded!
findings.body: `@loaded_locales ||= []` is performed outside any mutex. If two threads enter `ensure_loaded!` concurrently when `@loaded_locales` is still nil, each may assign a distinct empty array. The subsequent `load_locale` call acquires `LOAD_MUTEX` and appends to whichever array is current at that moment, but the losing thread's local reference (captured before the mutex) may point to the discarded array, causing a locale to appear unloaded on the next check. In practice MRI's GIL makes this unlikely to manifest, but under JRuby/TruffleRuby or with future Ruby changes it could cause a locale to be loaded twice or a check to incorrectly miss a loaded locale.

findings.title: ensure_loaded! acquires a mutex check on every request even when locales are already loaded
findings.body: `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` iterates over up to three locales and calls `I18n.ensure_loaded!` for each. Although `ensure_loaded!` short-circuits with an `include?` check before calling `load_locale`, it still performs the array lookup and method call overhead on every single request. For a hot path like `set_locale`, a simple guard (e.g., a boolean flag or checking `@loaded_locales` size against expected count) could avoid the per-request cost entirely after initial load.
